FXUS62 KRAH 101014
AFDRAH

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Raleigh NC
620 AM EDT Thu Sep 10 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...

* Limited cooling into the mid 80s to around 90 this weekend, with 
  heat returning Monday. 

* Risk for excessive rain lowering with the next (weakening) front 
  this weekend. 

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 155 AM Thursday...

1) Continued hot weather through Friday, with limited cooling this 
weekend. 

2) Marginal risk for excessive rain (flash flooding) on Saturday.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 155 AM Thursday...

KEY MESSAGE 1...  Continued hot weather through Friday, with limited 
cooling into the mid 80s to around 90 this weekend. 

Current observations and model data continue to suggest a weaker 
upper disturbance, stronger return of upper ridging more quickly, 
and a weaker cold front becoming stationary or washing out Saturday. 

Strong mid/upper level ridging will be overhead today and begin to 
shift off the south Atlantic coast Friday. This will allow a 
weakening cold front to push toward the region Friday afternoon and 
likely stall somewhere over central NC Friday night, then lift back 
as a warm front over the weekend. The upshot of all this will be the 
hottest day will occur today with very limited chance of PM 
convection. Highs in the lower to mid 90s. Heat indices will still 
be 100 or lower due to the dew points in the 60s. 

Dew points are forecast to rise into the lower to mid 70s Friday as 
the cold front approaches. There will be an increasing chance of 
showers/storms in the afternoon and evening. Highs will likely be a 
few degrees lower than today, offset by higher dew points. Heat 
indices of 98 to 105 NW to SE expected, with actual highs 90-95.

2) Marginal risk for excessive rain (flash flooding) on Saturday.

However, models continue to suggest a weaker upper disturbance, 
stronger return of upper ridging more quickly, and a weaker cold 
front becoming stationary or washing out Saturday. Excessive 
rainfall potential should be limited to isolated flooding and mainly 
in urban and poor drainage areas. Less QPF means little help with 
the current drought. 

Saturday will bring scattered thunderstorms with a low end excessive 
rainfall threat with the aforementioned helpful convective PM 
triggers. Limited shear should keep the storms from being organized 
and/or severe.
 
The return of strong upper ridging as early as Sunday means lower 
chance of PM thunderstorms Sunday into next week with increasing 
heat again, with highs Monday back in the lower to mid 90s. 

&&

.AVIATION /12Z THURSDAY THROUGH MONDAY/...
As of 620 AM Thursday...

Generally VFR conditions are expected through 12z/Friday. 

Outlook: A cold front will slowly work its way south from VA and 
potentially into NC Fri into Fri night. This boundary will likely be 
a focus for convection, but also bring a risk for post-frontal sub-
VFR cigs Sat morning. An approaching disturbance from the TN Valley 
and Deep South will bring a chance for more scattered to widespread 
showers/storms on Sat that may continue into early overnight period. 
A return to mainly VFR conditions are expected Sunday into early 
next week. 

&&

.RAH WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
None.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...Badgett
AVIATION...Badgett/AS

FXUS62 KILM 100958
AFDILM

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Wilmington NC
558 AM EDT Thu Sep 10 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Updated aviation discussion for 12Z TAFs.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
1) Shower and thunderstorm chances will increase this weekend 
as a storm system approaches the area.

2) Heat and humidity will build and heat indices could exceed
100 degrees yet again.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Shower and thunderstorm chances will increase 
this weekend as a front/system approaches the area. The 
somewhat zonal pattern that has been in place the past several 
days begins to amplify. Even today some sea breeze showers 
cannot be ruled out in the favored areas. By Friday a southwest 
flow will be in place as troughing develops and or moves into 
the Mississippi Valley. The slow moving nature of the system 
both the ridge and trough make slow progress make a soggy 
weekend in the offing. The usual caveat that it isn't going to 
rain all day or night holds here as well. 

KEY MESSAGE 2...Mid level ridging builds across the region again
next week after the unsettled weather. It appears the
temperatures have cooled both highs and lows under basically dry
conditions.

&&

.AVIATION /10Z THURSDAY THROUGH MONDAY/...
High confidence in mostly VFR conditions through 12Z Friday.
Confidence is a bit lower regarding fog/low clouds early this
morning (mainly at KFLO) and again late tonight (mainly at
KFLO/KLBT) as well as showers/storms into the evening (mainly
near the coast at KCRE/KMYR/KILM).

Extended Outlook... Although VFR conditions will prevail, there
is increasing potential for pop-up showers and thunderstorms
bringing brief MVFR/IFR conditions, especially Saturday and
Sunday. There is also a low potential for late night/early
morning stratus or ground fog, particularly affecting KLBT and
KFLO Saturday and Sunday.

&&

.MARINE...
Tonight through Monday...A southerly component will be in place
for the foreseeable future across the coastal waters. The 
southwest flow will not be particularly strong ten knots or 
less. Winds and seas may be distorted by convection at times 
especially this weekend with the higher pops. Significant seas 
will otherwise be 2-4 feet.

&&

.ILM WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
NC...Coastal Flood Advisory from 9 PM this evening to midnight EDT 
     tonight for NCZ107.
SC...Coastal Flood Advisory from 7 PM to 10 PM EDT this evening for 
     SCZ054-056.
MARINE...None.

&&

$$

FXUS62 KJAX 101128
AFDJAX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Jacksonville FL
728 AM EDT Thu Sep 10 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

For the latest NE FL and SE GA Daily Key Messages please visit:
https:/www.weather.gov/media/jax/briefings/nws-jax-briefing.pdf

- Moderate Rip Current Risk all Local Beaches Today and Friday. 
  Elevated Risk Returns Early Next Week.

- Daily Heat Index up to 107 through Sunday.

- Daily Afternoon & Evening Thunderstorms. Main Hazards: Locally 
  Heavy Rain, Lightning & Gusty Winds Up to 40-50 mph.

&&

.NEAR TERM /THROUGH TONIGHT/...

Main Highlights:

- Potential for a few strong thunderstorms and localized
  flooding this afternoon through early this evening, mainly at
  inland locations.

- Moderate Risk of Rip Currents Today. 

Some patchy fog early this morning inland areas, and can't rule 
out brief locally dense fog over inland southeast GA. Already 
seeing areas of low stratus so not a stretch to see a period of 
lower vsby there. Meanwhile, the pattern for today will pivot 
fairly quickly back to a southeast to south flow from 1000-700mb
as low level ridging moves offshore of the southeast states. A 
weak boundary, probably remnants of a frontal zone, will lift 
northward over the area today while dissipating, and be 
positioned near the Altamaha River Basin by about 2 PM. The 
airmass remains moist with PWATs of just over 2 inches per the 
18z JAX RAOB, with NAM and other guidance showing values near 
2.25 inches this afternoon. This moisture and daytime heating 
should result in MLCAPE of up to about 2500 J/kg, though deep 
layer shear remains weak. Isolated strong thunderstorms are 
still expected with gusty winds to about 50 mph and locally 
heavy rainfall. Max estimated max rainfall amounts may be near 4
inches in some spots. The more robust thunderstorms should be 
inland mainly near the U.S. Highway 301 corridor. Movement of 
the cells should be northerly about 10 mph by the afternoon. 
Isolated to scattered showers and storms expected this evening, 
but should dissipate through midnight as instability wanes. 
Patchy fog may develop once again late tonight inland areas.

Temperatures will trend above average with highs in the lower
90s  for most inland locations to upper 80s to near 90 at the 
coast. Peak heat index values will reach to about 106 or so 
today. Muggy overnight lows will range in the lower/mid 70s.

&&

.SHORT TERM /FRIDAY THROUGH SATURDAY NIGHT/...

Main Highlights This Period:

- Daily potential for isolated strong thunderstorms and
  potential for localized flooding.

Southwesterly to southerly steering flow will be in place
through  the period, bringing Gulf moisture across NE FL and SE
GA as PWATs rise to above 2.25". The steering flow will allow 
for the Gulf breeze to move well inland each afternoon, with 
mergers with the Atlantic sea breeze occurring between the 
US-301 corridor towards the I-95 corridor. With the elevated 
moisture aloft, showers and storms that do develop could bring 
periods of locally heavy rainfall. Isolated strong storms, maybe
a few severe storms, could bring gusty winds in the 30 to 50 
mph range. 

Daytime highs will be in the 90s along inland locations on
Friday and Saturday with highs in the upper 80s to lower 90s 
along the coast. Overnight Lows will be in the lower to mid 70s.
Heat index values will hover just under Heat Advisory criteria,
with values in the upper 90s to around 107F.

&&

.LONG TERM /SUNDAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY/...

Main Highlights This Period Saturday through Wednesday: 

- Above Average Temperatures & Daily Thunderstorms this Weekend. 

- Elevated Rip Current Risk Next Week. 

Relatively stubborn pattern will develop over the weekend and  
through next week as deep ridging becomes stacked well offshore. 
Initially over the weekend this positions a lower level ridge
axis directly across the local area, resulting in a weak 
southerly flow regime. The Gulf and Atlantic coast seas breezes 
are expected to push inland and trigger showers and storms as 
the breezes merge across inland areas during the late afternoon 
and into the evening. By Monday, the ridge axis moves north, 
reintroducing onshore flow early next week. The primary concerns
each day will be localized potential for strong thunderstorms 
due to mesoscale boundary collisions with the potential for 
localized rainfall and flooding concerns. With the return of 
easterly winds next week, local rip current risk will also 
become elevated once again. 

Temperature highs in the 90s will begin to decrease into the
middle of the upcoming week, with highs in the mid to upper 
80s as easterly flow returns on Tuesday. Lows will continue to 
range in the 70s.

&&

.AVIATION /12Z THURSDAY THROUGH 12Z FRIDAY/...

VFR conditions will prevail at the regional terminals through at 
least 17Z. Showers and thunderstorms will begin developing near 
the terminals towards 18Z, and TEMPO groups for brief surface 
wind gusts of 25-30 knots and IFR visibilities during heavier 
downpours were placed in the TAFs for the Duval County terminals
and GNV through around 01Z Friday. Confidence in impacts was 
slightly lower for the SSI and SGJ coastal terminals, where 
PROB30 groups for brief surface wind gusts up to 25 knots and 
MVFR conditions during heavier downpours were placed in these 
TAFs through around 00Z. VFR conditions should then prevail at 
the regional terminals by 02Z. Periods of LIFR to IFR conditions
are expected overnight at VQQ.

&&

.MARINE...

High pressure stretching across Georgia and the Carolinas will 
gradually weaken while shifting south through the weekend. 
Meanwhile, a cold front will move into the Ohio and Tennessee 
Valleys by Friday and move toward the area waters early next 
week.

Rip Currents: Diminished winds and dropping surf will tend to
lower  the rip current risk toward the moderate range today. 
Prevailing winds will become south-southwesterly by Friday, with
a lingering easterly ocean swell and onshore winds developing 
during the afternoon hours behind the inland moving sea breeze 
keeping a lower- end moderate risk at area beaches.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...

Winds will steadily veer to become southerly to southwesterly
Today.  This will allow for the Gulf Coast and Atlantic Coast 
sea breezes to push inland by the afternoon hours, with showers 
and storms developing and increasing in coverage near Highway 
301. As weaker transport winds develop, Dispersions will be Fair
for most of the time over the next few days. Otherwise, RH 
values will sit at Good levels through the weekend as moisture 
moves in from the Gulf and towards southeast Georgia and 
northeast Florida. 

Fog Potential: Gusty and erratic wind shifts will occur from  
thunderstorm activity. Patchy fog is expected across inland areas 
this morning, with widespread dense fog unlikely.

&&

.HYDROLOGY...

As far as coastal water levels, we expect tidal water levels to
peak  to near the Action stage through Friday due to the recent
onshore flow but mainly due to the new moon phase which is 
Friday, Sept 11th. Mostly nuisance type flooding is expected for
a brief time into the weekend, including in the St Johns River 
Basin.

As far as rainfall today, isolated pockets of about 4 inches are 
possible mainly across an area from eastern Marion county 
northward to around Baker county. These storms may cause 
temporary flooding, especially in any poor drainage or urbanized
areas.

&&

.PRELIMINARY POINT TEMPS/POPS...
AMG  92  73  91  73 /  40  30  50  10 
SSI  89  77  90  77 /  30  20  40  30 
JAX  91  74  92  74 /  60  30  60  20 
SGJ  90  75  90  75 /  50  20  60  10 
GNV  92  73  91  73 /  60  30  60  20 
OCF  92  74  91  74 /  50  30  70  20 

&&

.JAX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
FL...None.
GA...None.
MARINE...None.

&&

$$

000
FXUS65 KBOU 101106
AFDBOU

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Denver/Boulder CO
506 AM MDT Thu Sep 10 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Mainly dry through Friday with warmer temperatures.

- Return to more unsettled pattern this weekend with a chance of
  thunderstorms especially on Sunday. Cooler Saturday, then warmer
  on Sunday.

- Another cold front moves into the area next Monday or Tuesday
  with a chance of showers and thunderstorms.

&&

.DISCUSSION /Through Wednesday/...
Issued at 240 AM MDT Thu Sep 10 2026

The flow aloft will remain WNW today as southerly level flow is 
across the plains.  MLCAPE will rise up to 1000 j/kg over portions 
of the far ern plains by aftn.  Chances for tstms still look on the 
low side as I can't find a focus for activity.  However, can't rule 
out an isold storm or two mainly across Lincoln county where a weak 
convergence zone will exist this aftn.  Meanwhile, temps will begin 
to warm as readings reach the upper 80's to lower 90's over nern CO.

On Fri, zonal flow aloft will be over the area as a sfc lee trough 
develops over the plains.  This will lead to another warm day as 
highs rise into the upper 80's to mid 90's over the plains. 
Meanwhile, models have some mid level moisture embedded in the flow, 
which may lead to isold high based showers/tstms over the higher 
terrain in the aftn.  Across the plains, MLCAPE is under 500 j/kg so 
any threat of showers/tstms will be on the low side.

For Fri night into Sat, zonal flow aloft will continue.  Meanwhile, 
a cold front will move across Fri night into Sat morning.  This 
front will drop temps back to more seasonal levels across nern CO. 
MLCAPE is fcst to be in the 500-800 j/kg across the plains with 
lower values across the higher terrain.  For now, have kept in a 
slight chc for showers/tstms across the higher terrain and along the 
I-25 Corridor for the aftn/evening hours.  Highs over nern CO will 
be in the upper 70's to mid 80's.

By Sun, an upper level trough will move into the nrn Rockies with 
increasing WSW flow aloft across the area.  At the sfc, a lee trough 
will intensify east of the mtns with SSE low level flow across the 
plains.  MLCAPE is fcst to increase to 1000-1500 j/kg over portions 
of the plains east of a pseudo dryline. Thus may see a few 
strong/svr storms by late aftn thru the evening hours. Highs on 
Sun, will likely rise back to above normal levels.

Looking ahead to Mon, WSW flow aloft will remain over the area. 
Models have backed off on the timing of another cold front moving 
across as they now show it moving in Mon night into Tue morning.  If 
this front does hold off until Mon night, then another day of above 
normal temps would occur over the plains.  Meanwhile, may have a 
better chc of showers/tstms across the plains Mon night into Tue 
morning as position of upper level jet combines with upslope flow 
behind the front.  

For Tue, differences exist between the ECMWF and GFS with respect to 
timing of additional precip and temps.  The ECMWF has a cool and 
stable airmass, over the plains, with highs only in the mid 60's to 
lower 70s.  Meanwhile, the GFS isn't as cool and has far more 
precip.   

&&

.AVIATION /12Z TAFS through 12Z Friday/...
Issued at 504 AM MDT Thu Sep 10 2026

Light drainage winds will become light and variable by 16z. By 18z
winds will go ESE and then more SE by 23z. For this evening winds
will gradually become south by 03z and the SSW by 06z.  Otherwise
VFR conditions will continue thru the period.

&&

.BOU WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
None.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...RPK
AVIATION...RPK
